result.text:
The flight search engine is built in the running image, test-first: 14 new tests plus the 5 `TodasLasCombinaciones` tests you provided all pass (19/19). One exception to "see it fail first": test13 (several discounts are each taken off the gross cost) passed on its first run, because the design already worked that way. I kept it because the statement asks for that rule explicitly.

**Production classes** (in `2025-2C-Recuperatorio`):
- **`BuscadorDeVuelos`** is created with the flight definitions, the discounts and the passenger counter. It has three searches:
  - one-way: `viajesDeIdaDesde:hasta:el:para:`
  - round trip: `viajesDeIdaYVueltaDesde:hasta:saliendoEl:volviendoEl:para:`
  - multi-leg: `viajesPorTramos:para:`
  
  The first two just build the legs and use the multi-leg search. For each leg it keeps the flights that fly that day of the week and have enough seats. It combines the legs with `#todasLasCombinaciones` and drops any combination where a flight departs before the previous one arrives.
- **`Tramo`**: one leg of a search (origin, destination, date).
- **`DefinicionDeVuelo`**: a flight as defined (code, route, days of the week as a Chalten interval, departure time, duration, cost in dollars).
- **`Vuelo`**: a flight definition on a specific date. It knows its departure and arrival date and time.
- **`Viaje`**: what the search offers. It gives origin and final destination, departure and arrival, gross cost, net cost, and `descuentosAplicados`.
- **`Descuento`**, with the subclasses **`DescuentoPorFechaEspecial`** and **`DescuentoPorTramo`**: each is applied per leg, always over the gross cost.
- **`DescuentoAplicado`**: which discount was applied and how much it took off.

Tests are in `BuscadorDeVuelosTest`, in `2025-2C-Recuperatorio-Tests`, using the flights from the statement.

Decisions you may want to revisit:
- **Round-trip example:** the statement only lists AR100 + AR101. By its own rules IB300 + IB301 also fly those days (Dec 9 is a Tuesday, Dec 15 a Monday), so my test expects all four combinations.
- **Cost and passengers:** cost is the per-ticket price added up over the legs. It is not multiplied by the number of passengers, because the statement never says to.
- **Percentages:** written as whole numbers (`del: 10 porciento…` means 10%).
- **Passenger counter:** there is no real REST `ContadorDePasajeros` client, since no test could drive one. The buscador only needs an object that answers `asientosDisponiblesEnElVuelo:el:`, and the tests use `ContadorDePasajerosSimulado`.

I haven't saved the image or written the "2025" package to a file.
